caption:
Abu Dhabi's state oil company ADNOC signed a multi-year deal with OpenAI and G42 as Sam Altman visited the UAE.
It is the first energy company to deploy OpenAI Frontier, a platform for AI agents.
The first job: oil field development plans in hours instead of months, with human experts keeping oversight.

Would you trust AI agents to plan an oil field?

threads_text: OpenAI just signed up its first energy company: Abu Dhabi's ADNOC will use OpenAI's Frontier agents to plan oil fields, and says plans that take months could take hours. Humans still sign off on the big decisions. Would you trust AI agents to run parts of an oil company?

site_article.dek: The Abu Dhabi oil company plans to use AI agents for oil field planning and crude valuation, one of four OpenAI agreements signed in Abu Dhabi on November 2, 2026.

site_article.seo_title: ADNOC signs OpenAI and G42 deal to deploy Frontier AI agents
site_article.seo_description: ADNOC is the first energy company to deploy OpenAI Frontier. It will use AI agents for oil field planning and crude valuation, on G42 computing in the UAE.
site_article.answer_summary: ADNOC will use OpenAI Frontier, a platform for AI agents, to build oil field development plans and value crude from reservoir to sale, running on G42 infrastructure in the UAE. The deal value was not disclosed.
site_article.hero_alt: Officials in suits at a signing ceremony in Abu Dhabi, with a city skyline in the background.

paragraphs.text: The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, known as ADNOC, signed a multi-year agreement with OpenAI and G42 on Monday, November 2, 2026, and says it is the first energy company to deploy OpenAI Frontier. G42 signed through its subsidiary Inception42, according to The National. Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, witnessed the signing after meeting OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who was visiting the UAE.

OpenAI Frontier is a platform for building and managing AI agents that OpenAI launched in February 2026, The Next Web reported. Data Studios said it first went to a limited set of customers, with HP, Intuit, Oracle, State Farm, Thermo Fisher and Uber named as early adopters. ADNOC announced its part of the deal at ADIPEC, the UAE's largest oil and gas conference. Neither company disclosed the value of the agreement or a rollout date.
Oil field plans and barrel valuation

The first application is field master planning, which combines subsurface, facilities and economic studies into a development plan for an oil field. Those plans draw on data from thousands of wells, reservoirs and facilities, and ADNOC says the system could produce them in hours rather than the months the work takes today, according to The Next Web and Dubai Standard.

The second application values crude while it is still in the ground. AI agents would follow oil from the reservoir to the point of sale and forecast supply, demand, prices and margins, so that production, refining, sales and trading decisions are made together, The Next Web and Data Studios reported. ADNOC also said the platform will connect outputs from ENERGYai, its existing industrial AI system, which runs on a 70 billion parameter model trained on more than 50 years of company data.

ADNOC stressed that people stay in charge. The company said the platform will support its experts, who keep oversight of consequential decisions, according to ANI. The system runs on OpenAI's GPT models with inference hosted in the UAE on G42 infrastructure, The National reported. The deal also includes cybersecurity work under Daybreak Blue, OpenAI's program for vetted defenders, and training programs for ADNOC staff.

The agreement builds on earlier AI work at the company. ADNOC says ChatGPT Enterprise is already in use by more than 40,000 of its employees with adoption above 97 percent, and that it has more than 200 AI applications and 70 robotics use cases deployed or in development. Data Studios noted that these figures are reported by the company.

The ADNOC deal was one of four agreements between Abu Dhabi entities and OpenAI signed on November 2, covering government, energy and investment. The Abu Dhabi Government and OpenAI launched what they call an AI native Machine-Readable Government initiative, which converts policies and regulations into a format AI systems can read to help officials with compliance checks such as permits and certificates. Its first pilot, with the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority, focuses on food imports, and officials keep accountability for final decisions, The National reported.

Mubadala, Inception42 and OpenAI signed an agreement to apply AI to investment analysis, opportunity identification and risk assessment. Inception42 and OpenAI also signed a five-year agreement to support frontier AI adoption across government, enterprise and education in the UAE. Altman said Abu Dhabi and the UAE are setting a bold, global standard for AI integration across the public and private sectors, according to The National and ANI.

For OpenAI, the deal puts its agent platform inside one of the most data heavy industries, where planning errors are costly and decisions run across geology, engineering and trading. A national oil company that already gives ChatGPT Enterprise to tens of thousands of staff is also a customer that can deploy agents at scale. The emphasis on human oversight and UAE hosted inference reflects how cautious large industrial buyers remain about letting agents act on their own.
The next marker is the first published result from ADNOC's field master planning work, which will show whether the promise of plans in hours instead of months holds up on real oil fields.
